newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar falls on stop-loss sales in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls on stop-loss sales in Tokyo.

text.p: 2356 GMT --*Dollar dipped against yen in early trade, mainly on stop-loss dollar sales at 118.10 yen and 117.90 yen.
*But it was supported at around 117.80 yen due to commercial dollar buying ahead of local fixing at 0100 GMT and buying interest by some Japanese investors below 117.50 yen.
*Dollar in corrective phase after rising as high as 118.95 yen overnight, due to renewed concerns about U.S.-Japan trade relations.
*Further stop-loss dollar sales expected at 117.80 yen and 117.60 yen, said a dealer at a European bank.

*Traders in New York cited rumours that U.S. car markers wanted Washington to review U.S.-Japan trade barriers. *Opinions divided over dollar's direction in near term, with some saying that lingering concerns over Japan-U.S. trade dispute seen putting downward pressure on dollar.
*"Investors and exporters remained keen to sell dollars on rises on expectations that the dollar is unlikely to move out of the 110-120 yen range," said the European bank dealer.
*But Japanese bank dealers said expectations that Japan's low interest rates will continue and a surge in U.S. stocks to record-high levels could support underlying strength in dollar.
* "It's likely to consolidate its bottom and then resume rising towards 119 yen," said a trust bank dealer.
*U.S. fund operators, main driving force of dollar's rally in recent trade, expected to keep buying dollars on dips.

*"Exporters are still willing to sell dollars, but the fact is that buying demand is outpacing selling interest," said a Japanese city bank dealer."So I don't think the dollar's recent rally is over. There could be further scope to rise," he added.
*Hank Note, assistant general manager at Sumitomo Bank, said there is possibility that Japan's authorities will start verbal intervention to check dollar's rise at above 119.00 yen.
* "If the dollar passes 119 yen, its rise may not stop at 120 yen," Note said.
*Given that dollar broke through 200-day moving average and buying demand for dollar call options might have made authorities cautious about dollar's rise, he added.
*Traders said they would watch U.S. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for second quarter at 1230 GMT and job data on Friday.
*U.S. Wall Street pundits expect it to show economy expanded by 1.9 percent in first three months of the year against a neck-breaking 5.9 percent growth in the first quarter.
